A valise is a small bag used for carrying personal belongings — clothes, toiletries, and other essentials — when you travel. Think of it as a compact, hand-held travel bag, somewhere between a handbag and a small suitcase.

A valise is typically:

  • Small to medium in size — large enough to hold a change of clothes and a few personal items, but not big enough to pack for a long vacation
  • Rectangular or slightly rounded in shape, like a small suitcase
  • Carried by a handle on top, in your hand
  • Soft-sided, traditionally made of leather or sturdy fabric

A valise is meant for short trips — a night or two away from home. It holds just the basics: some clothes, toiletries, maybe a book. It's not meant for long journeys with a lot of luggage. Because of its compact size, it's easy to carry around, slip under a seat on a train, or take into a hotel room without hassle.
The feel and tone of the word

"Valise" is an older, somewhat formal or literary word. You're more likely to encounter it in classic novels, period films, or formal writing than in everyday modern conversation. If someone today said, "I packed my valise for the trip," it would sound slightly old-fashioned or elegant.

In modern everyday speech, people tend to use words like overnight bag, carry-on bag, travel bag, or just small suitcase instead. But "valise" is still understood and occasionally used, especially in writing.

• She arrived at the inn with only a small leather valise.
  • He threw a few shirts into his valise and caught the morning train.
  • The detective set his valise on the table and began unpacking his tools.
  • A valise sat by the door, packed and ready for her early departure.
A valise is a small, hand-carried travel bag used to pack personal items for a short trip — essentially a compact, old-fashioned version of what we'd today call an overnight bag.
